title: (RHBA-2015:0308) s390utils bug fix and enhancement update
portal_summary:
Updated s390utils packages that fix several bugs and add various enhancements
are now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.

relevant to your system have been applied.

portal_description:
The s390utils packages contain a set of user space utilities that should be used
together with the zSeries (s390) Linux kernel and device drivers.

The src_vipa component of the s390utils packages has been upgraded to upstream
version 2.1.0 which adds Internet Protocol version 6 support. (BZ#1088514)

This update also fixes the following bugs:

* As the s390utils-ziomon subpackage did not have explicit dependencies for all
required tools called by the ziomon code, Fibre Channel Protocol for System z
(zFCP) and Small Computer System Interface (SCSI) I/O performance analysis
failed. The missing dependencies have been added, and zFCP and SCSI I/O
performance analysis now succeeds. (BZ#1079474)  

* When the interface name argument was 16 or more characters, the qetharp
utility terminated unexpectedly with buffer overflow diagnostic. The check for
the argument size has been updated, allowing 15 characters at most, and qetharp
thus no longer crashes. (BZ#1081980) 

* Previously, removing a device that was currently offline resulted in an error.
The source code has been patched, and the "znetconf -r" command now removes
ccwgroup devices as expected. (BZ#1094382) 

* Prior to this update, the lsreipl code incorrectly set "fcp_dump" for FCP
re-IPL target instead of "fcp" regardless of the setting in the
/sys/firmware/reipl/reipl_type file. This bug has been fixed, and lsreipl now
displays FCP devices correctly. (BZ#1094383)

* The systemd daemon now uses a different configuration scheme to manage system
services and resources. As a consequence, the /etc/inittab file could not be
used to configure ttyrun or iucvtty instances. With this update, ttyrun and
iucvtty system instance units have been provided, thus fixing the bug.
(BZ#1098575) 

* Previously, if too long a string was passed as the interface name to the
quethqoat command, the buffer overflew and qethqoat terminated unexpectedly. The
length of the interface name is now checked to be in the range of allowed kernel
interface name lengths, thus fixing the bug. (BZ#1101262) 

* Previously, regular expression for the grep command could be expanded as a
wildcard. Consequently, when a file named "?" was present in the current working
directory, the system qeth device detection failed. This update puts the regex
argument of grep in single quotes, and files named "?" are now correctly
detected when the lsqeth command is run. (BZ#1107778) 

* Previously, the zipl virtblk heuristics incorrectly perceived SCSI backed
devices as Fixed Block Architecture (FBA) devices. The FBA heuristic has been
removed, and virtblk devices are now detected correctly. (BZ#1115980) 

* Previously, running the dbginfo.sh script collected only incomplete data. With
this update, data collection for systemd and lsdasd has been added to collect
complete data. In addition, the "-d" option has been added that allows to
specify a directory in which the collected data is stored. (BZ#1148732,
BZ#1148733, BZ#1087799) 

In addition, this update adds the following enhancements:

* The functionality of s390tools has been enhanced to allow to access z/OS
legacy data directly on the Direct Access Storage Device (DASD) storage devices
from a Linux system. The new "zdsfs" tool has been introduced to access the
content of IBM System z data sets and to provide certain meta data values.
(BZ#1088515)  

* This update adds support for System z OSA_Express5s cards to the qethqoat
tool. Besides recognition of the card, this feature adds the following new
functions: "QUERY_OAT" and "QUERY_CARD_INFO". (BZ#1088541) 

* The lszcrypt tool now reports Enterprise PKCS#11 (EP11) capability of
the CEX4S crypto adapter. (BZ#1088580)

* With this update, the hard-coded limit of 64 CPUs is removed from the cpuplugd
daemon. (BZ#1155717)

Users of s390utils are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix
these bugs and add these enhancements.
